config.title: Infrastructure as Code

intro.title: Infrastructure as Code
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll learn Infrastructure as Code (IaC) by creating a simple cloud server configuration using declarative code. You'll understand how IaC allows you to manage infrastructure through machine-readable files instead of manual processes. The core concept is treating infrastructure setup like software development—using version control, testing, and automation. You'll work with basic configuration files that define server properties and dependencies. This approach ensures consistent, repeatable, and scalable infrastructure deployments. By the end, you'll see how IaC reduces human error and speeds up environment provisioning.
intro.usecase: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) is the backbone of modern cloud infrastructure management, appearing in platforms like AWS CloudFormation, Terraform, and Azure Resource Manager. Developers use IaC to define entire server environments, networking configurations, and security policies through code templates instead of manual console clicks. This enables consistent deployment of production environments, automated scaling of web applications, and reproducible disaster recovery setups. In practice, you'll see IaC managing everything from Kubernetes clusters for microservices to complete CI/CD pipeline infrastructure, ensuring that every deployment is identical, version-controlled, and auditable.

objectives: Implement a basic Infrastructure as Code template using declarative syntax
Configure resource definitions for compute and storage components
Apply parameterization to make infrastructure templates reusable
Construct dependency relationships between infrastructure resources
Initialize a version-controlled repository for infrastructure code
Render infrastructure diagrams from code definitions
Update existing infrastructure configurations through code modifications

steps.title: Import the required modules for Infrastructure as Code
steps.instruction: Import the infrastructure definition module and the configuration module that will be used throughout this lesson.
steps.hint: Write two import statements at the top of your file to bring in the necessary modules.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the foundational modules imported and ready to use for Infrastructure as Code implementation.
successCriteria: Both the infrastructure definition module and configuration module are imported correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported both required modules: the infrastructure definition module and the configuration module.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports don't match what's needed. Please import both the infrastructure definition module and the configuration module.

steps.title: Define the main infrastructure configuration structure
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'defineInfrastructure' that returns an empty object. This will serve as the foundation for your infrastructure configuration.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure the function returns an empty object {}.

successCriteria: The function 'defineInfrastructure' is defined and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named 'defineInfrastructure' and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named 'defineInfrastructure' that returns an empty object {}.

steps.title: Initialize the infrastructure provider settings
steps.instruction: Inside your infrastructure configuration structure, add a provider configuration object that specifies the cloud platform as 'aws' and the region as 'us-east-1'.
steps.hint: Add a provider property with an object containing platform and region keys.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your infrastructure configuration should now include a provider object with platform and region settings.
successCriteria: The infrastructureConfig object contains a provider property with platform set to 'aws' and region set to 'us-east-1'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your provider object has both platform and region properties with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provider configuration is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add a provider object with platform: 'aws' and region: 'us-east-1' inside infrastructureConfig.

steps.title: Define the first compute resource
steps.instruction: Add a compute resource definition to your infrastructureConfig object, specifying instance type and basic properties.
steps.hint: Add a property like 'compute' to infrastructureConfig with an object containing instanceType and other properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The infrastructureConfig object now includes a compute resource definition with instance type and basic properties.
successCriteria: infrastructureConfig has a compute property with an object containing at least instanceType.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a compute resource, but it's missing required properties like instanceType.
steps.feedbackWrong: The compute resource definition is incomplete or missing. Ensure you add a compute property with instance type and basic properties.

steps.title: Define the networking configuration
steps.instruction: Add a networking property to your infrastructureConfig object that defines a VPC with a subnet.
steps.hint: Add a property named 'networking' to the infrastructureConfig object. This property should be an object containing a 'vpc' property (with a CIDR block) and a 'subnet' property (with a CIDR block).
steps.expectedOutcome: Your infrastructureConfig object will now include a networking configuration with VPC and subnet definitions.
successCriteria: The infrastructureConfig object has a 'networking' property containing 'vpc' and 'subnet' properties with CIDR block values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a networking property, but make sure it includes both 'vpc' and 'subnet' with CIDR block values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The networking configuration wasn't properly defined. Add a 'networking' property to infrastructureConfig with VPC and subnet definitions.

steps.title: Define storage resources
steps.instruction: Add a 'storage' property to your infrastructureConfig object with an array containing at least one storage resource definition. Each resource should specify a type (like 'block' or 'object') and a size (like '100GB').
steps.hint: Add a property named 'storage' to infrastructureConfig and set its value to an array of objects. Each object should have 'type' and 'size' properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your infrastructureConfig object will now include a storage property with an array of storage resource objects, each defining type and size.
successCriteria: infrastructureConfig has a 'storage' property containing an array with at least one object that has 'type' and 'size' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a storage property, but make sure it's an array with at least one object containing both 'type' and 'size'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The storage configuration isn't complete. Add a 'storage' property to infrastructureConfig with an array of objects specifying type and size.

steps.title: Create a resource dependency handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'establishDependencies' that takes the infrastructure configuration as a parameter and returns an object mapping resource dependencies.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts the config object and returns a new object showing which resources depend on others.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'establishDependencies' is defined that accepts the infrastructure configuration and returns dependency mappings.
successCriteria: The 'establishDependencies' function is defined with a parameter and returns an object showing resource dependencies.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named 'establishDependencies', accepts a parameter, and returns an object with dependency mappings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dependency handler function isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a function named 'establishDependencies' that takes the config and returns dependency mappings.

steps.title: Add security group definitions
steps.instruction: Inside the infrastructureConfig object, add a securityGroups property with an array containing at least one security group definition. Each security group should have a name, description, and inbound/outbound rules arrays.
steps.hint: Add a new property called 'securityGroups' to the infrastructureConfig object. The value should be an array of objects, where each object defines a security group with properties like name, description, inboundRules, and outboundRules.
steps.expectedOutcome: The infrastructureConfig object now includes a securityGroups property with at least one security group definition containing name, description, and rule arrays.
successCriteria: The infrastructureConfig object has a securityGroups property that is an array containing at least one security group object with name, description, inboundRules, and outboundRules properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a securityGroups property, but make sure it contains at least one complete security group object with name, description, and both inbound and outbound rules arrays.
steps.feedbackWrong: The security group definitions are missing or incomplete. Add a securityGroups property to infrastructureConfig with an array of security group objects, each containing name, description, inboundRules, and outboundRules.

steps.title: Define output values for infrastructure
steps.instruction: Add an 'outputs' property to your infrastructureConfig object to expose important resource attributes like IP addresses and resource IDs.
steps.hint: Think about what information would be useful after deployment - like the public IP of your compute instance or the ID of your storage resource.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your infrastructureConfig object will now include an outputs property that exposes key infrastructure information for use after deployment.
successCriteria: The infrastructureConfig object contains an outputs property with at least two output values (like IP addresses or resource IDs).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an outputs property, but consider adding more specific values like IP addresses or resource IDs that would be useful after deployment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The outputs property wasn't added correctly. Remember to add an 'outputs' property to the infrastructureConfig object with key-value pairs of important infrastructure attributes.

steps.title: Complete the infrastructure definition with validation
steps.instruction: Add a validation function that checks if the infrastructureConfig object has all required properties defined (provider, compute, network, storage, security, outputs).
steps.hint: Create a function named validateInfrastructure that takes the infrastructureConfig object as a parameter and returns true if all required sections exist, false otherwise.
steps.expectedOutcome: The infrastructure definition now includes a validation function to ensure completeness before deployment.
successCriteria: A validateInfrastructure function exists that checks for all required infrastructure sections and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a validation function, but it might not check all required sections. Make sure it validates provider, compute, network, storage, security, and outputs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation function is missing or doesn't properly check infrastructure completeness. Create a function named validateInfrastructure that returns true only when all required sections exist.
